titulo: The next day: check, measure, and create the new rule
lead: A night of queue is only worth it if the morning is short. You read the report in the chat, check each result against what you expected, note how many came out right on the first try, and turn the task that failed most into a new rule.
objetivo: check the night's batch, measure the first-try success rate, and write a rule for the task that failed most.
hero_alt: Morning with natural light, a cup of coffee, and a notebook with a list of results.

aprende.t: Where to look in the morning: chat, /status, and /jobs
The measure that matters: right on the first try
From failure to a rule in AGENTS.md or in the prompt
Your plan to complete the step

secoes.sub: Fifteen minutes that make the next night better.

nos.detalhe: Each task replied in the chat when it finished. Start by reading the conversation from top to bottom; /jobs and /completos show what finished, /status shows what is still open.
Open each result and compare it with the "Result you can check" column of your queue on paper. The question is simple: can you use it as is?
Count how many came out right without you touching them. That number, written down every morning, shows whether the queue is getting better or just running.

nos.sub: For the one that failed the most
nos.detalhe: Take the task that failed the most and write a one-line rule that would have prevented the mistake. It goes into the project's AGENTS.md or into the skill prompt. Run it again and compare.

secoes.volta: Tomorrow night already runs with the new rule
secoes.legenda: Click each block. Fixing by hand solves today; the new rule solves the nights to come.

rolagem_fim.texto: Read, check, measure, and turn the mistake into a rule. The agent does the work; you improve the process.

texto: Read the night chat. For each task you should have a result or a failure reason. A task with no reply at all is running or waiting: check it in /fila.
/completos lists the flows that finished; /status shows the ones that still need something from you (running or failed).
Open the file or the text and compare it with what you expected. Mark it: right on the first try, right with tweaks, wrong, or failed.
Don't fix anything yet. First look at the whole batch: the pattern of mistakes shows up when you see them all together.
Read the reason. código 143 was a restart, not an agent error: /refazer. Input error (broken link, wrong file): fix the input and send it again.
If the agent misunderstood, just redoing it the same way isn't enough: that's a case for a new rule.
A good rule is short, concrete, and testable: it says what to do, not only what to avoid. It goes into the project's AGENTS.md (step 1) or into the skill prompt.
Run the same task again with the rule and compare. If it got better, the rule stays; if not, rewrite it.

exemplo.texto: Meeting summaries: start with the decisions made and who is responsible, in at most 8 lines.

blocos.rot: Prompt for your agent to propose the rule
blocos.conteudo:
Read conferencia.md. For the task that failed the most:
1. Describe the error in one sentence, with an example of the result.
2. Propose ONE one-line rule, concrete and testable, for AGENTS.md or for the skill's prompt.
3. Tell me how I check tomorrow whether the rule worked.
Do not change any files; only propose.

abas.html:
Right on the first try: 7 of 10. Two right with adjustments (summaries too long) and one failure from a broken link.

New rule: "Meeting summaries: decisions and owners first, 8 lines at most."

The next night: 9 of 10.

• Fixing it by hand and not writing it down: the same failure comes back tomorrow.
  • Measuring only what failed: what matters is the share right on the first try.
  • Writing a vague rule ("be better"): there is no way to check it.
  • Restarting the bot while a task is still running to "clean up".

exercicios.texto: Fill in conferencia.md with each task from the night: result, whether it came out right on the first try, and what went wrong. Handle the failures by cause.
exercicios.pronto: each task in the batch has a line and you noted how many came out right on the first try.

exercicios.texto: Write a rule for the task that failed the most (in AGENTS.md or in the skill's prompt). Run the same task again the next night and compare.
exercicios.pronto: the rule is written, the task ran again, and you noted whether the result improved.

itens.texto: Durable queue: the request stays on disk, runs one at a time, resumes after a crash, and separates done from failed.
After what needs your eye and before what is costly or public. Read, fix, and only then approve.
Check, measure the ones right on the first try, and turn the failure that repeats most into a new rule.

The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: Which number should you write down every morning?
opcoes: How many messages the bot sent.
How many came out right on the first try, out of the total.
perguntas.explica: The share right on the first try shows whether the queue is improving. Sending more tasks says nothing about quality.

perguntas.p: A summary came out too long for the third night in a row. What should you do?
opcoes: Write a concrete rule in the skill's prompt or in AGENTS.md and compare the next night.
Switch the model without changing anything else.
Remove this task from the queue for good.
Shorten it by hand every morning.
perguntas.explica: Fixing it by hand solves today. The new rule solves the next nights and can be checked.

perguntas.p: A task failed with código 143. What goes into your check?
opcoes: A new rule for the agent.
Restart failure: /refazer and don't restart while a batch is running.
perguntas.explica: 143 means the service was shut down, not an agent error. A rule for the agent wouldn't fix it; the care goes into the restart.
